reason: This Hebrew text is the Sinai Covenant narrative (Exodus 19-32), which portrays the Hebrews as a recently liberated people receiving divine law and covenant in the wilderness, not as a nation engaged in political struggle. The passage explicitly references their past deliverance from Egypt ('אֲשֶׁר הֶעֱלָ֙נוּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם' - 'he who brought us up from Egypt'), showing liberation was already accomplished. The setting is Mount Sinai in the wilderness ('מִדְבַּר סִינַי'), not their own land. The narrative concerns theological covenant and law-giving, with the only conflict depicted being religious apostasy (the golden calf incident), not political struggle. The Hebrews are portrayed as receiving promises of their future land ('כָּל־ הָאָֽרֶץ' - 'all the earth'), but they are not yet positioned on their own land fighting for it.
